Out of Spec Worldbuilding Art Bible

Five starter tarantula morphs, three vertical mining biomes, and six eccentric colony neighbors—designed to plug straight into your MagicaVoxel queue, ChatGPT JSON schemas, and Grok dialogue drafts.

Starter tarantula roster and calibration outputs

Each morph rewards tighter indoor micro-climate control with a specific bio-material that unlocks deeper outdoor exploration. Early species forgive sloppy hygrometers; late-game alien morphs demand sub-degree thermal stability and pay off with elite satellite upgrades.

Morph Name Pedestal Substrate Climate Tolerance Precision Output Gameplay Unlock
1. Cobalt Sentinel Damp frontier moss & slate ±3.0 °C / ±8% RH Standard optical silk Cuts Day 1 tractor input lag by 25% when slotted into your dish.
2. Terracotta Knee Dry rust sand & shale ±2.5 °C / ±6% RH Anti-static dust filaments Slows rover steering-encoder drift during dusty surface harvests.
3. Crystal Weaver Bioluminescent gravel ±1.5 °C / ±4% RH Resonant emerald fibers Stabilizes mining drills so mid-tier canyon crystals do not shatter.
4. Orbital Silk-Spinner Chilled dark basalt ±0.8 °C / ±2% RH Zero-expansion reticle silk Unlocks multi-rover autopilot pathing across solar-flare days.
5. Basalt Thermal-Vent Heated volcanic slag ±0.4 °C / ±1.5% RH Mag-shielded thermal resin Lets rovers operate inside the deep magnetic dead-zone cavern.

Three vertical frontier biomes

Instead of one giant flat map, stack progression vertically. Every step deeper into the canyon trades clean orbital signal for rarer crystals, stranger substrates, and tougher calibration puzzles.

Tier 1 · Surface Plateau

Open twilight sky with reliable satellite line-of-sight (50 ms base lag). Ideal for starter crop plots, solar-charged mowers, and learning steering zeroing before boulders block your beam.

Tier 2 · Crystal Fault Terraces

Stepped canyon walls packed with cyan and violet ore veins. Cliff overhangs create moving signal shadows—forcing you to plant daisy-chained voxel relay poles and keep drills calibrated against rock vibration.

Tier 3 · Geothermal Dead Zone

Deep obsidian caverns lit by magma pools and emerald spores. Direct orbital signal is completely blocked; rovers must run pre-recorded autopilot routines buffered with thermal-vent tarantula resin.

The six quirky colony neighbors

Six distinct personalities are plenty to make the colony feel alive without burying you in dialogue trees. Every neighbor has a visible silhouette prop, a funny relationship with calibration, and a clear mechanical reason to visit them.

1. Bram

Scrapyard Rover Mechanic

Fixes rovers with percussive maintenance and zero respect for torque specs. Trades upgraded treads, bigger batteries, and illegal signal boosters for canyon scrap.

2. Dr. Lin

Colony Botanist & Substrate Dealer

Terrified of spiders on Day 1, fascinated by your optical silk by Day 15. Buys frontier crops and sells exotic mosses that unlock higher-tier tarantula morphs.

3. Inspector Vance

MegaCorp Compliance Auditor

Arrives via drop-pod every fifth morning with a glowing amber clipboard. Issues absurd fines for crooked calibration stickers—unless you bribe him with pristine traceability logs.

4. Kestrel

Hooded Orbital Trader

Shows up only during solar-flare nights beside a humming mystery crate. Sells rare off-world tarantula slings and gray-market reference standards.

5. Chet

Rival Calibration Contractor

Wears a blinding neon vest and "eyeballs" every measurement. Constantly brags about his fake ISO certificates while secretly hiring you to fix his botched colony jobs.

6. Old Orin

Retired Canyon Geologist

Knows every crystal vein and magnetic dead zone below the plateau. Teaches you how to place underground relay beacons in exchange for calibrated thermal probes.

“Hand the tarantula table to ChatGPT for your JSON stats, hand the six neighbor bios to Grok for dialogue, and keep this art bible open while blocking out MagicaVoxel.”

Every creature, biome tier, and colonist now maps directly to a concrete system inside your Godot 4 vertical slice.
